prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1002; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for side impact collision at intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a vehicle that failed to yield at a controlled intersection. Police report requested. Claimant reports wrist fracture and has retained counsel, who has requested all future communication be directed to their office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and receive initial medical authorization forms. Attorney indicates the claimant underwent surgical reduction of a wrist fracture and expects a lengthy recovery. Requested copies of all treatment records and bills to date. No liability admission made at this time.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Responding officer noted the at-fault driver's signal was red for the opposing direction at the time of impact. Witness statement obtained from a pedestrian at the corner confirming the other vehicle entered the intersection late. Liability appears clear. Recommended that the at-fault carrier be contacted for coordination of bodily injury claim.

Entry 4: Contacted at-fault carrier's adjuster. They acknowledged the claim and stated coverage is confirmed under the at-fault driver's policy. Discussed the injury claim scope. Their adjuster requested the claimant's medical records before evaluating settlement value. Forwarded requests to claimant's counsel for response.

Entry 5: Received medical records from claimant's attorney, including orthopedic consult notes and imaging reports showing a displaced wrist fracture. Treatment plan includes physical therapy and a follow-up in several weeks. Reserves reviewed and adjusted for bodily injury exposure. File flagged for supervisor review due to attorney involvement and injury severity.
